source.title: Implicit bias of gradient descent for mean squared error regression with wide neural networks

record.tranche_reason: The paper develops an implicit-bias account of regression fits, but does not test held-out generalization or any listed claim version.
record.gate_note: The paper reports zero training error and convergence toward spline solutions, but no measured training–test gap, test error, or result for V1–V8. Those findings are recorded as outside the listed versions. Cited generalization results are not extracted as this study’s results.
record.test_reason: The study characterizes the implicit bias of wide shallow networks in regression. Its width-dependent errors measure distance to a variational spline solution, not test error. Section 3.3 connects these results to cited spline approximation bounds as sample size increases, but neither those arguments nor the numerical illustrations test V1–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. More precisely, the authors characterize initialization-dependent implicit bias in wide shallow regression networks: smoothness is penalized relative to the initial function, with spline solutions under specified conditions. They argue that the resulting effective capacity, governed by sample size, can explain generalization and describe training trajectories approximately through smoothing splines.
record.recipe_differences: Theoretical analysis and numerical illustrations of wide shallow ReLU networks on regression; it does not use the classification, optimizer, batch-size, regularization, sharpness, or memorized-example procedures in the claim versions.
record.method_sensitivity: The implicit-bias description depends on initialization distribution; the paper also distinguishes standard from NTK parametrization and discusses the effect of linear adjustment.

fits_no_version.finding: Under the stated assumptions, trained univariate networks approach interpolants minimizing an initialization-dependent weighted squared curvature of the change from the initial function, with uniform discrepancy Op(n^−1/2).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient descent on sufficiently wide shallow ReLU regression networks implicitly selects spline-like interpolants determined by initialization.

fits_no_version.finding: For multivariate regression, the limiting interpolant minimizes a weighted squared Radon-transform penalty on a fractional Laplacian of the change from initialization; specified initializations yield polyharmonic splines.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gradient descent on sufficiently wide shallow ReLU regression networks has an initialization-dependent multivariate spline characterization.

record.problems: The paper’s numerical illustrations compare trained functions with variational solutions rather than reporting held-out errors. The generalization discussion relies on spline approximation results and cited work; the supplied text reports no direct test-set measurement for the claim versions.
record.rows_left_out: No results omitted. The paper’s cited prior-work results were excluded.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label generalization, including chance-level held-out accuracy for random labels.
Whether test error decreases as width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Image-classification performance of convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.
Held-out performance of adaptive optimizers versus SGD under different tuning or weight-decay recipes.
Batch-size effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets and adapted training recipes.
Dropout's effect on held-out error across data sizes, dropout strengths, and augmentation conditions.
Magnitude-aware parameter sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and comparisons with other measures.
Test-accuracy changes after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: The record overstates the absence of generalization analysis: Section 3.3 explicitly transfers cited spline approximation results to the proposed characterization. These concern target-function approximation as sample size increases, not the width-versus-test-error comparison in V2. Input-space curvature is also distinct from the parameter sharpness named in V7.

versions.untested_parts: Natural-label versus random-label training and held-out accuracy.
Test error as width increases past the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers.
Adaptive optimizers versus SGD and held-out performance.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to the training–test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring test accuracy.
